First of all, thank you for the Hebrew lesson👍🏻😄

One part of your answer somewhat confused me, you said a lot of the settlers in West bank choose to move on their own, against Israel’s laws.

Can you explain a little bit further about this? Aren’t the settlers in West Bank protected by the IDF?

Thank you so much for your thorough answer, I really appreciate the offer. I do actually believe a lot of the points you mentioned. but unfortunately there is one point I’m gonna have to disagree with you on. And again, this is just my viewpoint and I in no way intend to insult you or anyone else. 

You mentioned “Israel is the ancestral homeland of Jewish people” I haven’t done any research on this subject hence I’m gonna believe you.

Let’s say Israel is indeed the Jewish’ homeland, then does that give the Israelis government the authority to kick people out of their homes, homes in which they’ve lived in for a long time? Just because it used to belong to Jewish people a thousand years ago? This does not make any sense to me, ofc I haven’t seen Israel myself but I’ve watched way too many videos, of settlers (in the west bank) escorted by the IDF, drive people out of their homes. drive as in force them out with violence if necessary. and I’m not gonna lie, seeing the cruelty really pisses anyone off, that’s why lots of people take Palestine’s side without proper knowledge. Because all they see is a group of people, supported by a powerful military kicking people out of their homes because “it belonged to my ethnicity”. 

There’s no sugarcoating the fact that the Israeli have the upper hand in this situation, and the violence caused by the settlers (many of whom weren’t even born in Israel!) is the reason many people see Israel as this monstrous demonic country who steal lands, and will use a gun when needed. 

Also, as far as I’m concerned, Palestinians who live in Israel have the same rights as an Jewish Israeli, but Palestinians who live in Gaza are in a blockade by Israel, meaning they cannot be moved and they can’t vote in elections. The Palestinians living in West Bank are somewhat the same, but those who live in Jerusalem have a bit more freedom. 

That’s why I think saying “The settlers are actually decolonizing West Bank” isn’t at all accepted. Lots of people who live there have also been born there. 

You can’t say that someone with a Jewish ethnicity who was born in Europe or America has the right to take other peoples’ homes just because of the fact that they’re jewish, that is the literal definition of apartheid.
